messages:
maria: Customer reported intermittent 5-10s tail latency spikes on /v1/embeddings after we rolled out a dynamic-batching tweak to maxtune earlier today. They also saw a few "Dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768" errors for some batched requests.

sam: Can you paste the exact request headers and model? which embedding model/version are they calling?

maria: They call model `embed-large-v2` (pinned v2026-02). Example header: `x-client-id: acme-analytics`, requests are mixed single and 2-item batches via our SDK. Request sample: ```json
{"inputs": ["short text"], "model": "embed-large-v2"}
```

maria: Customer log shows this sequence: one large burst of tiny requests + periodic 2-item requests. Suspect dynamic batching coalesced requests from different client SDK versions (one uses 768-dim fallback) -> mismatch at coalescing time.

jia: Interesting. embed-large-v2 should be 1536 dims. Where would a 768-dim payload come from? Are they using an older local SDK or a 3rd party wrapper?

maria: They confirmed one microservice was still on SDK 0.9.1 (we require 1.2+ after vector-dim change). Customer admits a canary svc hadn't been updated.

lin: Repro plan: 1) simulate two clients: one requesting 1536-dim embed, one sending 768-dim (simulate older SDK). 2) Hit dedicated pool with dynamic batching enabled and maxtune config currently `max_batch_size: 64, dynamic_batching: enabled, maxtune_threshold: 0.15`. 3) Observe coalescer validation and tail latencies.

sam: Also capture the coalescer logs around request_tag / req_id. If mismatch gets through, we need to check the batch validator that enforces per-batch uniform dimension. Should reject incompatible requests instead of trying to pack them.

maria: Customer supplied two failing request_ids: `req_2026_78a3c` and `req_2026_78a4d`. Server logs snippet attached: 
```
ERROR [coalescer] req_2026_78a3c: payload_dim=768 != model_dim=1536 -> batch_reject
WARN [batcher] created batch b-4096 size=3 latency=3120ms
ERROR [inference] req_2026_78a4d: processing failure: kv-cache index OOB
```

sam: That kv-cache OOB could occur if the runtime applied 1536-length KV indexing to a 768 vector — looks like a failing input validation earlier would have prevented this.

jia: Quick mitigation: set `dynamic_batching: disabled` on affected pool to force per-request execution (reduces tail spikes but increases avg cost). Also reduce `max_batch_size` from 64 -> 16 as a short-term safety.

lin: I can push a temporary policy to the customer's dedicated pool. Want me to do that now?

maria: Yes please — customer is on a P1. They'll take the short-term perf hit. Please include a note to tell them to update their SDK to >=1.2 and to flush any in-flight cached requests.

deploy-bot: deploy started: update-pool-config pool=acme-dedicated user=lin change="dynamic_batching: disabled; max_batch_size: 16" (deploy id dpl_2149000001)

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: dpl_2149000001 (30s)

lin: Done. Confirmed pool policy applied; metrics show immediate drop in 95th percentile from ~4.8s -> ~450ms.

maria: Customer reports errors stopped and tail spikes gone. They will roll forward SDK and re-enable dynamic batching once all services are on 1.2+.

sam: Follow-up action items: 
- Add stricter pre-coalesce validation to reject mismatched-dim requests earlier and log client sdk version if present.
- Add telemetry counter for "batch_dim_mismatch" and alert when >5/min per pool.
- Add a safety gate: if batch validator sees >1 distinct dim in queue, either split into compatible batches (preferred) or fail fast with clear error to client.

jia: I'll own the batch-splitting change and a unit test matrix for mixed-dim streams. Estimate ~2 dev days + 1 day test.

sam: I'll own the validator + telemetry alert. Will spec a runbook for SRE to toggle dynamic batching and maxtune quickly.

lin: I'll add to oncall checklist: if "batch_dim_mismatch" alert -> set dynamic_batching=disabled + reduce max_batch_size while we triage.

maria: Thanks team. Closing loop with customer now. :thumbsup:
__metadata_note: This thread is a single-string Slack conversation. Messages are chronological and prefixed by sender. No title field per agents.md.
